# Service Design Package (SDP) Templates

**← Back to [EAP Home](../../../README.md) • [Resources](../../README.md) • [Work Templates](../README.md)**

---

> This directory contains Service Design Package (SDP) templates for comprehensive IT service documentation. The SDP framework provides a standardized approach to documenting requirements, design, build, test, operations, migration, and security considerations for enterprise applications and services.

[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#purpose]

### Purpose

The Service Design Package (SDP) framework provides comprehensive documentation for IT services throughout their lifecycle, from initial requirements through operations and maintenance. Each SDP serves as the authoritative technical documentation for an application or service.
page_texts.5:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Comprehensive Documentation**: Single source of truth for all technical aspects of an IT service
- **Standardized Approach**: Consistent structure and content across all applications
- **Operational Excellence**: Detailed runbooks and monitoring guidance for reliable operations
- **Risk Management**: Security considerations and compliance documentation
- **Knowledge Preservation**: Captures critical technical knowledge and decisions
- **Audit Readiness**: Complete documentation trail for compliance and governance
page_texts.6:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#scope-and-applicability]

### Scope and Applicability

SDPs are applicable for:

- ✅ **New Application Implementations**: Complete documentation for greenfield projects
- ✅ **Legacy System Migrations**: Migration planning and new system documentation
- ✅ **Major System Upgrades**: Updated documentation for significant changes
- ✅ **Service Handoffs**: Operational transition from development to production support
- ✅ **Compliance Documentation**: Audit and regulatory requirement documentation

[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#when-to-create-an-sdp]

### When to Create an SDP

Create a Service Design Package for:

1. **New Application Development**: All new applications require a complete SDP
2. **Major System Changes**: Significant modifications that impact architecture, security, or operations
3. **Migration Projects**: Systems being migrated or replaced need updated SDPs
4. **Compliance Requirements**: When detailed technical documentation is required for audit or regulatory purposes
page_texts.16:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#phase-1-planning-and-preparation]

#### Phase 1: Planning and Preparation

1. **Project Scope Definition**
   - Identify the application/service scope
   - Determine stakeholders and reviewers
   - Establish documentation timeline

2. **Template Preparation**
   - Download the main SDP template from the assets section above
   - Download required appendices based on system complexity
   - Review reference examples for guidance
   - Select appropriate runbook templates based on your platform (DHCF, GainwellOne, or migration scenarios)
   - Customize placeholders with actual project information
page_texts.17:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#phase-2-content-development]

#### Phase 2: Content Development

3. **Requirements Documentation** (Appendix B)
   - Document all functional and non-functional requirements
   - Establish requirements traceability
   - Link to project management tools (ALM, Azure DevOps)

4. **Design Documentation** (Sections 3, Appendices C-L)
   - Complete technical design sections
   - Develop architectural diagrams and models
   - Document system configurations and dependencies

5. **Build and Configuration** (Section 4, Appendices M-N)
   - Document all configuration items
   - Create detailed configuration guides
   - Establish CMDB entries
page_texts.18:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#phase-3-testing-and-operations]

#### Phase 3: Testing and Operations

6. **Test Documentation** (Section 5, Appendix O)
   - Create comprehensive test cases
   - Document test results and validation criteria
   - Link to test management systems

7. **Operations Documentation** (Section 6, Appendices P-Q)
   - Develop operational runbooks
   - Create monitoring and alerting procedures
   - Document support processes and escalation paths
page_texts.19:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#phase-4-security-and-migration]

#### Phase 4: Security and Migration

8. **Security Documentation** (Section 8, Appendix T)
   - Complete security risk assessment
   - Document access controls and audit procedures
   - Establish compliance documentation

9. **Migration Planning** (Section 7, Appendix R)
   - Develop data migration strategies
   - Plan user migration and training
   - Create rollback procedures
page_texts.20:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#review-and-approval]

### Review and Approval

- **Technical Review**: Enterprise Architecture and technical teams
- **Security Review**: Information Security team review of security considerations
- **Operational Review**: Operations team review of runbooks and monitoring
- **Stakeholder Approval**: Business stakeholders and project sponsors
- **Governance Approval**: Architecture Review Board or equivalent governance body

page_texts.23:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#introduction-section-1]

#### Introduction (Section 1)

- **Purpose**: SDP objectives and alignment to project standards
- **Service Description**: High-level overview of the IT service and its business purpose
page_texts.24:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#requirements-traceability-matrix-section-2]

#### Requirements Traceability Matrix (Section 2)

- **Requirements Documentation**: Complete listing of functional and non-functional requirements
- **Traceability**: Links between requirements, design elements, and test cases
- **Lifecycle Management**: Requirements change management and version control
page_texts.25:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#design-section-3]

#### Design (Section 3)

- **Technical Architecture**: Overall system design and architectural patterns
- **Platform Specifications**: Hardware, software, and infrastructure requirements
- **Integration Design**: Interfaces, APIs, and system connections
- **Data Architecture**: Data models, flows, and storage considerations
page_texts.26:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#build-section-4]

#### Build (Section 4)

- **Configuration Management**: All configuration items and their relationships
- **Deployment Architecture**: Environment specifications and deployment procedures
- **Infrastructure as Code**: Automated provisioning and configuration scripts
page_texts.27:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#test-section-5]

#### Test (Section 5)

- **Test Strategy**: Testing approach and methodologies
- **Test Cases**: Comprehensive functional and non-functional test scenarios
- **Validation Criteria**: Acceptance criteria and success metrics
page_texts.28:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#operations-section-6]

#### Operations (Section 6)

- **Operational Procedures**: Day-to-day operations and maintenance tasks
- **Monitoring and Alerting**: System health monitoring and incident detection
- **Performance Management**: SLA metrics and performance optimization
- **Support Procedures**: Troubleshooting guides and escalation processes
page_texts.29:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#migration-plan-section-7]

#### Migration Plan (Section 7)

- **Data Migration**: Strategies for data transfer and transformation
- **User Migration**: User account creation, training, and transition plans
- **Rollback Procedures**: Contingency planning for migration issues
page_texts.30:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#security-considerations-section-8]

#### Security Considerations (Section 8)

- **Access Control**: Authentication, authorization, and role-based security
- **Data Protection**: Encryption, privacy, and compliance measures
- **Audit and Compliance**: Logging, monitoring, and regulatory alignment
- **Threat Management**: Security risks and mitigation strategies
page_texts.32:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#documentation-quality]

#### Documentation Quality

- **Completeness**: All required sections and appendices documented
- **Accuracy**: Technical details verified and validated by subject matter experts
- **Clarity**: Clear, actionable language appropriate for target audience
- **Consistency**: Follows established templates and enterprise standards
page_texts.33:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#technical-quality]

#### Technical Quality

- **Architecture Alignment**: Consistent with enterprise architecture principles and standards
- **Integration Standards**: Proper interface design and API specifications
- **Security Compliance**: Meets security standards and regulatory requirements
- **Operational Readiness**: Comprehensive operational procedures and monitoring

page_texts.35:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#critical-path-appendices]

### Critical Path Appendices

These appendices are typically required for most SDPs:
page_texts.36:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#-high-priority-always-required]

#### 🔴 **High Priority** (Always Required)

- **Appendix B (RTM)**: Requirements traceability is mandatory for all projects
- **Appendix D (System Config)**: System specifications required for deployment
- **Appendix P (Runbooks)**: Operational procedures critical for service support
- **Appendix T (Security)**: Security documentation required for compliance
page_texts.37:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#-medium-priority-usually-required]

#### 🟡 **Medium Priority** (Usually Required)

- **Appendix C (Significant Realizations)**: Important for complex architectures
- **Appendix G (Network Diagrams)**: Required for infrastructure-dependent services
- **Appendix I (Interfaces)**: Necessary for integrated systems
- **Appendix O (Test Cases)**: Required for quality assurance
page_texts.38:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#-low-priority-conditional]

#### 🟢 **Low Priority** (Conditional)

- **Appendix E/F (Software)**: Required when using non-standard software
- **Appendix R (Migration)**: Only for migration projects
- **Appendix S (User Roles)**: For applications with complex user management
page_texts.39:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#appendix-dependencies]

### Appendix Dependencies

Some appendices have dependencies on others:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Appendix B - RTM] --> C[Appendix C - Significant Realizations]
    C --> O[Appendix O - Test Cases]
    D[Appendix D - System Config] --> G[Appendix G - Network Diagrams]
    D --> E[Appendix E - Standard Software]
    D --> F[Appendix F - Non-Standard Software]
    G --> H[Appendix H - Network References]
    I[Appendix I - Interfaces] --> L[Appendix L - Data Models]
    P[Appendix P - Runbooks] --> Q[Appendix Q - Supporting Documentation]
    R[Appendix R - Migration] --> S[Appendix S - User Roles]
    T[Appendix T - Security] --> H
```

page_texts.42:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#content-guidelines]

#### Content Guidelines

- **Be Specific**: Provide concrete details rather than generic statements
- **Include Examples**: Use real examples and sample configurations
- **Version Everything**: Track changes and maintain version history
- **Link Appropriately**: Cross-reference related sections and external documents
page_texts.43:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#template-customization]

#### Template Customization

- **Remove Unused Sections**: Delete sections that don't apply to your service
- **Add Project Context**: Customize placeholders with actual project information
- **Maintain Consistency**: Use consistent terminology and formatting throughout
- **Update TOC**: Ensure table of contents matches actual content structure
page_texts.45:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#stakeholder-engagement]

#### Stakeholder Engagement

- **Early Involvement**: Engage stakeholders during initial template customization
- **Regular Reviews**: Schedule interim reviews for complex SDPs
- **Clear Ownership**: Assign clear responsibility for each section and appendix
- **Expert Validation**: Have subject matter experts review their domain sections
page_texts.46:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#review-process]

#### Review Process

- **Structured Reviews**: Use formal review processes with defined criteria
- **Parallel Reviews**: Allow multiple reviewers to work simultaneously on different sections
- **Consolidate Feedback**: Use a single person to consolidate and resolve conflicting feedback
- **Track Actions**: Maintain an action log for all review feedback and resolutions
page_texts.48:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#lifecycle-management]

#### Lifecycle Management

- **Regular Updates**: Update SDPs when system changes are implemented
- **Annual Reviews**: Conduct annual reviews to ensure accuracy and relevance
- **Version Control**: Maintain clear version control with change documentation
- **Archive Management**: Properly archive outdated versions while maintaining access
page_texts.49:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#continuous-improvement]

#### Continuous Improvement

- **Feedback Collection**: Gather feedback from SDP users and reviewers
- **Template Evolution**: Update templates based on lessons learned and best practices
- **Process Refinement**: Continuously improve the SDP creation and review process
- **Knowledge Sharing**: Share successful practices and lessons learned across teams

---
page_texts.50:
[resources/work-templates/service-design-package/README.md#-getting-started]

## 🔍 Getting Started

1. **📋 Review Requirements**: Understand project scope and documentation requirements
2. **📁 Browse Templates**: Review the template structure above to understand available templates and appendices
3. **📚 Review Examples**: Study completed reference examples for guidance
4. **📝 Download Templates**: Download appropriate templates and appendices for your service
5. **🔧 Choose Runbook Template**: Select the appropriate runbook template based on your platform:
   - DHCF platform: Download DHCF V01 template
   - GainwellOne platform: Download GainwellOne template
   - Migration projects: Download DHCF to GainwellOne mapping template
6. **✏️ Customize Content**: Customize downloaded templates with project-specific information
7. **👥 Engage Stakeholders**: Involve relevant teams in content development
8. **🔍 Review and Validate**: Conduct thorough reviews with subject matter experts
9. **✅ Obtain Approvals**: Complete formal review and approval processes
10. **📚 Maintain Documentation**: Keep SDPs current throughout the service lifecycle
